newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia cement plant reopens after rebel attacks.
newsitem.headline: Colombia cement plant reopens after rebel attacks.

text.p: Production has restarted at Colombia's third largest cement plant after leftist rebel attacks forced it to close for six weeks, the company chairman said Monday.

Cementos Rioclaro shut down and laid off 350 workers in mid- October after the National Liberation Army (ELN), the country's second largest guerrilla force, dynamited 13 electricity pylons which supplied the plant in Puerto Triunfo, in northwest Antioquia province.

The attacks came in the wake of the company's refusal to pay the rebels hefty "war taxes" -- a payment frequently demanded by guerrillas from industrialists to prevent their operations being sabotaged.

"Those who carried out the attacks have decided to allow the peaceful continuation of Cementos Rioclaro's activities...There are neither victors nor vanquished. The community, the respect for freedom and brotherhood have triumphed," chairman Luis Fernando Ochoa said in a press statement.
The Cementos Rioclaro plant has a production capacity of 1.3 million tons of cement annually. But a slump in the construction industry has cut demand.
Ochoa has consistently said the company does not pay war tax to the ELN but it does spend about 200 million pesos ($200,000) a year on social programs in the area.
